id: # V3 DIARIZATION AUDIT — fill in the 20 rows at the bottom. ~40 min.
# Play audit clips A01-A20 (2 min each). They are mid-episode: the first
# 120s of every episode is skipped so intros and ads don't flatter the result.
# WHAT YOU ARE JUDGING: how much of each clip is the HOST talking. Not the
# content, not a transcript. The measured rate is fingerprint-words per HOST
# word — if guest speech leaks into the host column the denominator is wrong.
# COLUMNS TO FILL:
#   host_pct       0-100. Host's share of the TALKING. Nearest 10 is fine.
#   who_dominates  HOST / GUEST / EVEN. Use EVEN for roughly 40-60.
#   third_voice    Y if you hear anyone who is neither host nor guest
#                  (audience, producer, a played clip, a co-host). Else N.
#   notes          anything odd: music, ad read, crosstalk, phone audio,
#                  long silence. If you cannot tell which voice is the host,
#                  write that — 'indistinguishable' is a real finding.
# host_name is pre-filled per row, so you never have to infer who the host is.
# era is here only so I can check accuracy doesn't differ between periods.
# Don't let it influence your listening.
# THE ONE RULE: do not open answer_key.json until you are done. It holds the
# pipeline's answers. Blind labels are the only kind worth having — if you've
# seen the machine's answer the gate becomes unfalsifiable.
# Two of the twenty are episodes an automated QA rule flagged as implausible
# (pipeline claims ~99.9% host). They are unmarked on purpose. Your blind
# labels on those two decide whether they're excluded from the analysis.
# Don't try to guess which ones they are.
# OUTCOMES: gate is host-attribution accuracy >=90%. PASS = corpus validated.
# FAIL = diarization isn't fit for purpose and the pilot reports that as a
# finding — that is a real result, not a mistake on your part.
# Partial is usable. 12 clips gives a wider interval but still works.
# Send the file back with whatever you have. Leave these # rows in place.
